title: KV cache + quantization onboarding notes (weekly)
content:
Week notes (Jul 21-22, 2026) - quick capture

Context:
- Goal: get a 13B-class open model (customer-requested variant) into the Redwood catalog with an int4 quantized execution profile and KV-cache friendly runtime path. Keep production perf within SLOs (<= 90ms/ token warm for common seq lengths) and latency regression < 10% vs float16 baseline for short responses.
- Work split across: quantization experiment (Ravi), runtime changes for KV cache streaming + eviction (Liam), onboarding checklist + eval harness (Anya), CLI/infra infra tests (Sofia).

Standup highlights (Jul 21):
- Ravi: AWQ int4 pass. Compression: model size down ~3.1x. Throughput: ~2.6x tokens/sec improvement on A100 for batched decoding compared to fp16 (with caching disabled). Noted small quality drop on multi-hop QA prompts.
- Anya: Eval harness expanded to include our canonical regression set + new prompt family (multi-hop reasoning + chain-of-thought). Observed MRR drop ~4.8% on the reasoning set for int4 AWQ baseline compared to fp16. Need targeted calibration.
- Liam: KV-cache eviction bug repro: when sequence length crosses threshold 512->1024 in streaming, cache pointers misalign after a rollout test (repro in canary). Leads to silent token duplication ~rare but reproducible with long-prefill + streaming. Patch in review.
- Sofia: Added infra job to run compile+profile for quant variants nightly; discovered compilation time for int4-kernel selection increases 2.2x (CI timeout). Will bump timeout and move heavy builds to dedicated runners.

Quick experimental details:
- Test model: community-13b-v2 (ops: attention + rotary embeddings).
- Quant methods tried: AWQ (int4), GPTQ (int4 fast), Mixed 4/8 hybrid.
- Preliminary numbers (evaluation harness, short-answer subset, 200 prompts):
    - fp16 baseline: avg latency 72 ms/token (warm, batch size 1), mem 12.2 GB, EM-like score on QA-set: 0.712
    - AWQ int4: avg latency 68 ms/token, mem 4.0 GB, EM-like score: 0.678
    - GPTQ int4: avg latency 66 ms/token, mem 4.2 GB, EM-like score: 0.689
  Notes: latency improvements modest for single-token streaming due to kernel overhead; major wins are memory and throughput for batch workloads.

Evaluation observations and hypotheses:
- Quality regressions concentrate on long-context reasoning prompts where per-head scale matters; hypothesize small scale collapse in key layers after coarse quantization.
- Mixed 4/8 hybrid (keeping earlier attention blocks at 8-bit) recovers ~60% of the lost EM while keeping mem <6GB. Worth profile.
- Token-level logit shifts visible for AWQ on thermometer prompts (calibration drift). Consider tiny post-quant calibration (bias-corr) or final-layer float copy.

Onboarding checklist items (current status):
- [x] Model artifact retrieval + integrity checks (sha256 verified)
- [x] Tokenizer compatibility test (vocab match, unknown token rate <0.5%)
- [x] Basic smoke run (generation sanity)
- [~] Quant profile generation (nightly job started; first profiles available)
- [~] Kernel selection matrix (partial; int4 kernels need explicit fallback to mixed-precision for head ops)
- [ ] Evals: full multi-task suite (regression + generation + embeddings)
- [ ] Runtime rollout plan: canary -> regional fallback -> full (need SRE signoff)
- [ ] Monitoring: add quality-regression alerts tied to baseline prompt-set (Anya owner)

Blockers and risks:
- KV-cache pointer bug blocks safe streaming rollout for models > 512 prompt length. Patch in PR but needs load tests. Impact: customers using long-chat flows may see duplication.
- Int4 kernel compilation / timeout causing CI noise; need infra runner allocation and flaky-retry backoff.
- Potential licensing/footprint issue: model variant uses a tokenization mapping edge-case; flagged legal for review (low priority but must be tracked).

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Ravi: run mixed 4/8 quant sweep focusing on first 6 attention layers by Fri 2026-07-24; push best config to PR with per-prompt diffs.
- Anya: extend eval harness to include 1k long-context prompts and calibrate EM thresholding; deliver preliminary dashboard by Mon 2026-07-27.
- Liam: finish KV-cache pointer patch + add stress test for streaming long-prefill paths; aim for canary re-run Wed 2026-07-23.
- Sofia: create dedicated CI runner pool for heavy quant+compile jobs and increase job timeout; ETA Tue 2026-07-28.
- Maya: coordinate SRE signoff thread and draft rollback playbook for canary.

Meeting notes (deep-dive, Jul 22):
- Discussed three mitigation approaches for quality regressions: 1) mixed-precision selective layers, 2) post-quant EM-fitting (small calibration dataset), 3) lightweight finetune/LoRA on top of quantized weights. Consensus: try (1) + (2) first due to lower infra cost.
- Runtime strategy: prefer to keep same API surface but expose two model profiles ("nominal-quant" and "high-quality-hybrid"). Routing rule: short queries -> nominal-quant, reasoning/long -> high-quality-hybrid. Need routing signal experimentation.
- Canary plan: start with 2% traffic in us-west-2, monitor token-level deltas + end-to-end latency distribution + error traces. Auto-fallback: immediate fallback to fp16 on detected token duplication or EM drop > 8% for the prompt family.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Instrument token-level perplexity in streaming path to detect drift early.
- Add small synthetic prompts that stress attention symmetry (we saw failure modes there).
- Revisit kernel selection code path to allow fallthrough to mixed-precision for heads without recompiling entire model. Might save CI time.

Misc links and refs (copied for convenience):
- quant PR: https://github.com/redwood-research/quantization/pull/412
- CI job: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/quant-nightly-22
- Jira: AMPL-231 (model onboarding), AMPL-247 (kv-cache streaming bug)

Next syncs:
- Short sync M/W/F for standup updates (15m). Deep-dive Thu (30m) to validate canary criteria.

-- end of capture --
